translations.10: In the workspace, the place that everyone can see is called the "Commons" (ひろば).
translations.11: Anyone can post notes in the plaza.
translations.12: Ms. Takanashi shares her sales schedule in the plaza every morning.
translations.13: You can invite members to the workspace by email.
translations.14: Invited people will receive a confirmation email.
translations.15: Once an administrator approves, you can join right away.
translations.16: Member permissions can also be changed for each plaza.
translations.18: Notes are saved automatically and synced across all your devices.
translations.19: You can edit offline, and they sync as soon as you reconnect.
translations.2: Memot is a note app that lets you combine text, tables, and images all in one place.
translations.20: You can restore a previous version from the page history.
translations.21: Ms. Yamanashi recovered the text she had accidentally deleted.
translations.23: It's convenient to pin important pages.
translations.24: Pinned pages appear at the top of the list.
translations.25: Notes in the plaza become easier to find when you add tags.
translations.28: The same tag can also be used for a single word.
translations.29: In search, you can also look for both Hiroba and Hitokoto at the same time.
translations.3: This guide explains using the examples of Yamanashi-san from public relations and Takanashi-san from sales.
translations.30: If you can't find what you're looking for, try widening the search range.
translations.4: A short note added to a page is called a "Quick Note" (ひとこと).
translations.5: Yamanashi-san records the decisions from the meeting in the Quick Note.
translations.6: Yamanashi-san puts sticky notes on important parts to mark them.
translations.7: You can add up to ten comments per page.
translations.9: Takanashi-san's sales team first created a workspace.
